title: Dungeon layout planner: winding sloped halls, side rooms, shafts, room roles (pure Core data)
player_outcome: Groundwork for a Terraria-style dungeon: long winding brick halls stepping down toward the caverns, side rooms, vertical shafts, and rooms with roles (library, treasure, barracks, spike pit, vault, a bound prisoner). It is planned deterministically per seed and sized to the world.
design: New folder src/Strata.Core/WorldGen/Structures/Dungeon/.
DungeonLayout.cs types:
enum HallKind { Flat, Stairs, Shaft }.
record DungeonHall(Id, Start, Dir (axis unit; (0,−1,0) for shafts), Length, Kind, Width, Height, FromNode, ToNode) with Interiors() (one box per stair step for Stairs) and FloorY(k).
enum RoomKind { Keep, Junction, Hall, Library, Treasure, Barracks, SpikePit, Vault, Mechanic, Alcove }.
record DungeonRoom(Id, Interior, Kind, Node, PanelStyle 0..2, Doorways).
DungeonLayout { KeepInterior, Door, Inward, Halls, Rooms, Nodes, Edges, ChestSpots (with a ShadowKey flag), MechanicCell, VaultRoom, Bounds, Hash() }.
DungeonSite: Gate, Inward (the axis toward the world centre), WorldSize, LayerBands, Func surface(x,z), Func landness(x,z).

DungeonBudget.For(WorldSizePreset): Tiny {halls 260 cells, rooms ≥ 6, locked chests 4, branches 2, floor ≥ CavernTop−10}; Small {700, 14, 8, 5, CavernTop−40}; Medium {1200, 22, 12, 8, CavernTop−60}; Large {1800, 30, 16, 11, CavernTop−80}. Never below UnderworldTop+40.
DungeonPlanner.Plan(site, budget, SeedTree seeds) uses named streams 'dungeon.trunk', 'dungeon.branches' and 'dungeon.roles', so later tweaks do not reshuffle the layout.
Trunk walk from the keep shaft's bottom. Kind weights: flat 0.5, stairs 0.35, shaft 0.15 (only while above the floor limit).
Direction: keep the heading (0.5) or turn ±90° (0.25 each). Never head outward (dot with Inward < 0).
Lengths: flat 16–40, stairs 12–28 (1:1 descent along the axis), shaft 16–32 deep.
Segment cross-sections: interior width 7, height 9 (the player is 3.6 cells tall); shafts 8×8.

Each segment must fit: inside the world with a 12-cell margin; top ≤ surface − 12 sampled every 6 cells (except under the keep); floor ≥ budget floor; no interior overlap with earlier interiors in a coarse 8³ occupancy grid, except at the joining node.
On an invalid segment, try up to 6 alternatives, then stop the walk.

At each node: a room with probability 0.45 (14–26 × 10–16 × 14–26 interior; roles by quota: 1 library per 4 rooms, treasure until the chest quota, barracks, 1 spike pit per 5), otherwise a junction widened 1.4×.
Branches: at nodes with probability 0.3 while branches remain, walk 80–160 cells ending in a Treasure or Library room.
Side rooms: 35% of flat halls ≥ 24 long get an Alcove or Treasure room on one side, joined by a 3×5 doorway.

Post-pass: convert junctions/alcoves until quotas are met. The deepest room becomes the Vault. The room nearest the median depth becomes Mechanic. Chest spots: one per Treasure room plus alcove extras; exactly one has ShadowKey.
All integer math, axis-aligned, no trig (worldgen determinism).
tests: DungeonLayoutTests over seeds 1..24, Tiny and Small (all plan-only, fast):
MeetsItsQuotas: rooms ≥ min, chest spots ≥ quota, exactly one ShadowKey, one vault, one mechanic room, ≥ 1 library.
verification: dotnet test; check_file_length (keep the planner files < 300 lines each)
risks: Tiny worlds (512³, LandRadius ≈ 215) are cramped. The planner must degrade gracefully (fewer rooms) rather than fail. Tests assert the Tiny quotas.
The occupancy grid may reject too much and leave short dungeons. Log the achieved budget in the worldgen-report tool.
